newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Deputy Prime Minister Amnuay Viravan confirmed yesterday he will head NAP's economic team if the party wins the election and seek five cabinet seats for his appointees. Amnuay said the team would include Narongchai Akaraserani, president of General Finance & Securities Plc, and other businessmen he did not name. (BANGKOK POST)

-Intimidation row intensifies. NAP leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh warned the Democrat Party yesterday against dragging the military into politics following claims that men in uniform were intimindating cavassers and candidates of NAP's rival upcountry. Democrats, however, became even more adamant in their claims. Party secretary-general Sanan Kachornprasart charged that intimindation and harrassment by the NAP had become more rampant and he vowed to seek immedidiate meetings with the Army and the supreme commander to discuss the problem. (THE NATION)

- A poll by the Mathichon newspaper-TV Channel 3 and INN radio station shows that the Democrat Party will win the November 17 election with 125 seats, followed by the New Aspiration party that is expected to win 109 seats. The three news organisations sent teams to questions voters nationwide and found that the Democrats would win the election. (MATHICHON)

- BoI calls for one-year delay in tariff cuts. The Board of Investment wants import tariff cuts, due next year, to be delayed by twelve months to avoid worsening the hardship of several industries through cheaper imports. The board headed by Prime minister Banharn Silpa-archa yesterday agreed to ask the Finance Ministry to delay the cuts, board secretary-general Staporn Kavitanond said. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thailand asks Apec for lowest-possible tarriffs. Thailand wants Asia Pacific leaders to offer a down-payment in the form of lowest tarrif commitments possible for the end of Apec trade and investment liberalisation, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Amnuay Viravan said.

Amnauy said Thailand's liberalisation offer to Apec would go beyond its commitment to the WTO, but he noted that Thailand still considered the Asean Free Trade Liberalisation Agreement as its priority. Thailand wants to create an AFTA agreement with the highest degree of liberalisation cooperation (THE NATION)
